page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable cloud instance based on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, supporting 2 threads per core. Memory capacity stands at 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an extensive instruction set encompassing AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 extensions, and SHA-NI cryptography. The instance includes no local storage and relies on external block storage, with baseline networking throughput rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance alongside moderate multi-threaded efficiency. In Geekbench tests, the instance records a single-core score of 2172.0, placing in the top quartile, while multi-core throughput scores 4953.0. Single-threaded data handling excels, evidenced by strong gzip compression speeds of 34.54 GB/s and bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.48 GB/s. However, multi-core sustained processing exhibits limitations inherent to its burstable allocation and two-physical-core topology, with multi-core stress-ng performance falling into the lower quartile at 4334.16.

Application and synthetic subsystem benchmarks show consistent mid-tier capability across memory and transaction testing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 41.23 GB/s and write bandwidth yields 29.77 GB/s, aligning with PassMark memory scores of 2111.34. The instance handles 7.8 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves 8.75 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Machine learning execution remains entry-level, processing small 135M language model prompts at 557.2 tokens per second and text generation at 179.75 tokens per second.

As a burstable flex tier offering, Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.xlarge balances resource density and economical compute capability for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it lacks bundled local disks and dedicated GPU acceleration, it represents a cost-efficient profile for web serving, microservices, lightweight application backends, and intermittent batch processing rather than sustained heavy parallel compute.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. It delivers 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate competitive single-core execution, achieving 2172.0 in Geekbench single-core and 34.54 GB/s in gzip compression. Multi-threaded capacity reflects its burstable CPU allocation and two-core foundation, producing average results in compiling, image processing, and Redis caching tests. The architecture supports modern instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. This instance provides a cost-efficient operational profile for non-sustained compute tasks, static web serving, staging environments, and entry-level database applications.
